account: This morning appears quiet so far. I read today's appointment book and met the secretary for office business. No new correspondence or urgent concerns have reached me. The secretary visited the mill yesterday evening and early today but could not find the miller; that is worth following up during my ten o'clock grain inspection, although I do not know why the miller was absent. The baker and neighbour reported no firsthand mill concerns, so I have no evidence of a problem there. The neighbour confirmed our usual three o'clock tea at the riverside cottage and said nothing urgent needed attention. Builder is now in the office, and the secretary has asked whether there is business or a concern to record. I have not heard Builder's answer and cannot yet say what brings them here. The secretary is staying available for callers while I prepare to leave for the mill. My remaining scheduled business is lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea at three, office at half past four, and home at seven.
